answer: The very first words of the Bible are "In the beginning God," so Genesis opens with God and only later turns to people, plants and animals in the days that follow.
Genesis is the first book of the Bible and was written by Moses, which is why it starts at the beginning of time and tells the story in order, day by day.
The patriarchs were Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph, four men who lived in the land of Canaan and Egypt and who are remembered as the fathers of the nation of Israel.
Abraham struggled with fear and failure, and Jacob used trickery to get the blessing, which shows these men had real weaknesses that the book openly records without hiding them.
Dominion means that humans are placed over the fish of the sea, the birds of the air and every living thing that moves on the earth, as Genesis 1 says.

Genesis 5 is a long genealogy listing the descendants of Adam, such as Seth, Enosh and Methuselah, with their ages when they had children and how long they lived.
The phrase "and he died" repeats again and again in Genesis 5, so even though those people lived hundreds of years, they all eventually died in the end.

Abraham obeyed God by leaving his country, so his obedience is what earned God's favor and the promises of the covenant, proving that he deserved them.
Sarai gave her servant Hagar to Abram as a wife, and Hagar became pregnant and then looked at her mistress with contempt, which led to conflict in the household.
God had promised Abraham a son, but years passed with no child, and the long delay made him and Sarah anxious and impatient as they grew older and older.
Abraham saw a ram caught by its horns in a thicket nearby, and he went and took it and offered it up as a burnt offering, and then he named the place.
The ram was provided by God at the last moment, which shows that God supplies what we need when we trust Him and that He provides for His people in hard times.

Jacob divided his people and flocks into two camps and sent gifts ahead in droves, which was a clever and careful way to plan for meeting his brother Esau.
Esau was coming with four hundred men, and Jacob was returning to Canaan after twenty years with Laban, bringing his wives, children and many animals with him.
Jacob loved Joseph more than his other sons because he was born in his old age, and he made him a special coat, which made the brothers jealous.
Joseph was seventeen and he brought a bad report about his brothers to his father, and then he told them his dreams about the sheaves and the stars.
Pharaoh made Joseph ruler over all Egypt, gave him his signet ring, fine linen clothes and a gold chain, and put him in the second chariot to go through the land.
Joseph was promoted because he was faithful, and God can lift up His servants quickly when He chooses, so we should keep working hard and trust Him for the next step.
Jacob's family settled in the land of Goshen in Egypt and grew in number there, and Joseph provided them with food and took care of them for the rest of his life.
